statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 12 (low) with the Globex reopen trading two-way inside a roughly 43-point band and no volatility premium rebuilt overnight.
recommendation: Tail at 12 maps to EA_ON under the fixed repository mapping. The 22:00Z Globex reopen has produced an orderly, narrow, two-way tape rather than a continuation of Monday's record-setting one-way advance, and that observed path - not the size of Monday's move - is what the Tail score reflects. On present evidence the mapped state is projected to stay at EA_ON overnight and at or below WATCH through the Tuesday US session, with the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z Richmond Fed, Williams and Jefferson cluster forming the narrow danger window to 16:00Z. Tail remains below the blocking threshold across the entire published 24-hour path.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures reopen flat in a narrow two-way band after Monday's record AI-led advance
body: Monday's US cash session ended with the Nasdaq-100 at 30,482.35, up 2.83% and 75 points under its 30,557.33 session high, while the Nasdaq Composite set a record close at 27,122.09 (+2.26%), the S&P 500 closed at 7,764.70 (+1.49%) and the Dow at 52,048.83 (+0.71%). Participation was uniform: the PHLX Semiconductor Index rose about 4.3%, all eight tracked megacaps and all seven tracked semiconductors finished the latest session higher, with Meta up 11.3%, Arm about 17%, Intel about 12%, Qualcomm 9.3% and AMD near 10% as it passed a $1 trillion market value. The decisive current evidence, however, is the Globex reopen. CME equity-index futures came back at 22:00Z and NQ has since traded near 30,800, roughly +0.1%, inside a band of about 30,778 to 30,821 on two independent delayed feeds - a narrow, balanced tape with no directional efficiency and no extension of Monday's one-way advance. That is the single most relevant observation for mean-reversion conditions, and it is why Tail is scored at 12 rather than at the levels reached intraday on Monday. Cross-assets are risk-supportive but not aligned into a trend: the 10-year yield fell about 4 basis points to 4.96% after touching a 19-year high of 5.041% last week, the 2-year is near 4.75%, and the 18 September H.15 carries 4.76% and 5.01%. WTI fell 4.8% to about $95.45 and Brent 3.8% to about $99.93 in a fourth consecutive losing session, on hopes of US-Iran contact at the UN General Assembly. VIX finished at 14.87, essentially unchanged on a 2.8% index day, so the advance carried no volatility confirmation and no volatility premium has been rebuilt overnight. Shared Finviz context was partial again this cycle, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so its breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections were used only as latest-session confirmation and no cross-asset futures alignment was read from it. The week ahead is thin on data and heavy on Fed communication: Richmond Fed, Williams and Jefferson on 22 September, flash PMIs on 23 September, jobless claims on 24 September, and the Trump-Xi state visit in Washington from 23 to 25 September with the White House bilateral and state dinner on 24 September as the largest unscheduled-headline source of the week.

lookbackSummary: Over the preceding 24 hours Tail traced a full arc from 6 in the quiet Sunday-night and Asian hours to a peak of 33 during the US afternoon, as a broad AI-led advance held the index near session extremes with aligned megacap and semiconductor participation. The published series ran green through 10:00Z, yellow from 11:00Z, orange from 14:00Z to 19:00Z, then stepped back to yellow at 23 once the 20:00Z cash settle removed the opening-auction continuation mechanism, and to green at 14 during the maintenance halt. Stress followed the same path from 34 to a 57 peak before easing to 38, and Confidence improved from 75 to 90 as live evidence accumulated, then eased to 85 when the futures tape went dark.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the low band across the entire overnight cycle, troughing at 10 through the Asian afternoon, then lifting into the watch band for the Tuesday US session with a peak of 23 in the 14:00Z window that covers the cash open aftermath and the Richmond Fed, Williams and Jefferson cluster. Mapped policy state is projected to stay at EA_ON overnight and to reach WATCH only between 13:00Z and 17:00Z, never touching the blocking threshold on current evidence. The narrow danger window spans 13:30Z to 16:00Z on 22 September. The invalidations that would lift Tail beyond this path are an opening-auction continuation with shallow or failed retracements, the index holding near fresh extremes, or a delayed second leg after front-end repricing around the 17:00Z 2-year auction and Barkin remarks.

The balanced, narrow reopen follows Monday's 2.83% NDX advance to 30,482.35 but shows no directional efficiency, so Tail is scored at 12 in the low band.
